**Sikhae (Seaweed Soup) – A Quick & Healthy Korean Dish** *This simple recipe serves about 2–3 people.* --- ### Ingredients | Item | Amount | |------|--------| | **Kelp (seaweed)** | 1 sheet (about 5 cm × 15 cm) | | **Water** | 4 cups (≈ 950 ml) | | **Soy sauce** | 1 tablespoon | | **Sesame oil** | 1 teaspoon | | **Garlic** | 1 clove, minced | | **Green onion** | 1 stalk, sliced into thin rings | | **Optional add‑ins** | • ½ cup diced tofu
• ½ cup sliced shiitake mushrooms
• 1 small carrot, julienned | --- ### Equipment - Medium saucepan - Small bowl for soaking kelp - Strainer (optional) --- ### Instructions 1. **Prep the Kelp** - Rinse the kelp under cold water to remove excess salt. - Cut it into bite‑size strips (about 1 cm wide). - Place the strips in a small bowl with 1 cup of water; let them soak for ~10 minutes. This softens the kelp and reduces the strong sea flavor. 2. **Boil the Base** - In a medium saucepan, bring the remaining 3 cups of water to a gentle boil. - Add the soaked kelp along with the soaking liquid. - Reduce heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes. If you’re adding mushrooms or carrots, toss them in now so they soften but keep their shape. 3. **Season** - Stir in soy sauce, sesame oil, and minced garlic. - Let the soup continue to simmer for another 2–3 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed (more soy sauce for saltiness, more sesame oil for aroma). 4. **Add Optional Extras** - If using tofu, add the cubes at this point and simmer for an additional minute until heated through. - Sprinkle sliced green onions over the top just before serving. 5. **Serve** - Ladle the hot soup into bowls. - Enjoy immediately while it’s steaming—perfect as a light starter or side dish. --- ### Tips & Variations - **Flavor Boosters**: Add a pinch of sugar or a splash of rice wine for depth. - **Protein Upgrade**: Replace tofu with diced chicken breast or shrimp for a heartier meal. - **Texture Play**: Toss in some sliced zucchini or spinach during the last minute of simmering for extra greens. - **Storage**: Leftovers keep well in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat gently on the stove or microwave. Enjoy your homemade *sikhae*! It’s quick, nutritious, and captures the clean, umami taste of the sea.
